claim: The cell envelope of Gram-negative bacteria consists of two membranes surrounding a periplasm and peptidoglycan layer.
source: The cell envelope of Gram-negative bacteria consists of two membranes surrounding a periplasm and peptidoglycan layer.
evidence: This is a well-established fact about Gram-negative bacterial cell structure, representing established scientific knowledge.

claim: In Escherichia coli, the coiled-coil lipoprotein Lpp contributes the only covalent linkage between the outer membrane and the underlying peptidoglycan layer.
source: In Escherichia coli, the coiled-coil lipoprotein Lpp contributes the only covalent linkage between the outer membrane and the underlying peptidoglycan layer.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about E. coli cell envelope structure.

claim: Lengthening Lpp to the upper limit does not change the spatial constraint but is accommodated by other factors which thereby become essential for viability.
source: Using proteomics, molecular dynamics, and a synthetic lethal screen, we show that lengthening Lpp to the upper limit does not change the spatial constraint but is accommodated by other factors which thereby become essential for viability.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from proteomics, molecular dynamics simulations, and synthetic lethal screens presented in the manuscript.

claim: E. coli expressing elongated Lpp does not simply enlarge the periplasm in response, but the bacteria accommodate by a combination of tilting Lpp and reducing the amount of the covalent bridge.
source: Our findings demonstrate E. coli expressing elongated Lpp does not simply enlarge the periplasm in response, but the bacteria accommodate by a combination of tilting Lpp and reducing the amount of the covalent bridge.
evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulations showing tilting and proteomics data showing reduced Lpp+21 levels.

claim: Very few proteins need to be up- or down-regulated in steady-state levels in order to accommodate the longer Lpp.
source: by quantitative proteomics discovered that very few proteins need to be up- or down-regulated in steady-state levels in order to accommodate the longer Lpp.
evidence: This is supported by the quantitative proteomics data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Lpp+21 strain shows increased levels of factors determining cell stiffness.
source: We observed increased levels of factors determining cell stiffness, a decrease in membrane integrity, an increased membrane vesiculation and a dependance on otherwise non-essential tethers to maintain lipid transport and peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by the proteomics data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Lpp+21 strain shows a decrease in membrane integrity.
source: We observed increased levels of factors determining cell stiffness, a decrease in membrane integrity, an increased membrane vesiculation and a dependance on otherwise non-essential tethers to maintain lipid transport and peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by the SDS sensitivity assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Lpp+21 strain shows increased membrane vesiculation.
source: We observed increased levels of factors determining cell stiffness, a decrease in membrane integrity, an increased membrane vesiculation and a dependance on otherwise non-essential tethers to maintain lipid transport and peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by the OMV quantification data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Lpp+21 strain shows a dependence on otherwise non-essential tethers to maintain lipid transport and peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
source: We observed increased levels of factors determining cell stiffness, a decrease in membrane integrity, an increased membrane vesiculation and a dependance on otherwise non-essential tethers to maintain lipid transport and peptidoglycan biosynthesis.
evidence: This is supported by the synthetic lethal screen data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Recent work investigating the spatial demands for assembly of proteins into the outer membrane has shown precincts of active protein integration into the membrane can deliver new material to the growing outer membrane (Gunasinghe et al., 2018).
source: Recent work investigating the spatial demands for assembly of proteins into the outer membrane has shown precincts of active protein integration into the membrane can deliver new material to the growing outer membrane (Gunasinghe et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior published work.

claim: Random planar movement from protein integration precincts drives the observed non-uniform distributions of the major proteins of the outer membrane (Rassam et al., 2015; Ursell et al., 2012).
source: random planar movement from these precincts drives the observed non-uniform distributions of the major proteins of the outer membrane (Rassam et al., 2015; Ursell et al., 2012).

claim: Elements of the LPS-transport machinery (e.g. the Lpt complex) (Freinkman et al., 2012; Sperandeo et al., 2017; Sperandeo et al., 2011; Ekiert et al., 2017; Shrivastava and Chng, 2019) span the OM and IM in order to fulfil their function in delivering lipid components to the outer membrane.
source: elements of the LPS-transport machinery (e.g. the Lpt complex) (Freinkman et al., 2012; Sperandeo et al., 2017; Sperandeo et al., 2011; Ekiert et al., 2017; Shrivastava and Chng, 2019) span the OM and IM in order to fulfil their function in delivering lipid components to the outer membrane.

source: In both cases, extending the coiled-coil structure of Lpp by 21 residues (Lpp+21) was found to be the longest form that supported close to normal growth (Cohen et al., 2017; Asmar et al., 2017).

claim: Imaging of Lpp+21 strains showed that the total periplasmic width had been stretched ~3–4 nm (Cohen et al., 2017; Asmar et al., 2017).
source: Imaging of these Lpp+21 strains in both studies showed that the total periplasmic width had been stretched ~3–4 nm (Cohen et al., 2017; Asmar et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: Lpp is 78 residues in most species of bacteria including E. coli.
source: A phylogenetic assessment of Lpp lengths across diverse bacterial lineages showed a very narrow window of protein size (Figure 1A), with Lpp being 78 residues in most species of bacteria including E. coli.

claim: Lpp lengths of 99 residues or more are at the upper end of the natural range for this protein and are found in the genus Geobacter.
source: Lpp lengths of 99 residues or more are at the upper end of the natural range for this protein and, in nature, these longer Lpp proteins are found in the genus Geobacter.
evidence: This claim is supported by the phylogenetic analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The Lpp+21 isoform expressed in E. coli sits near the upper physiological range observed among bacteria.
source: The previously described Lpp+21 isoform expressed in E. coli therefore sits near the upper physiological range observed among bacteria.

claim: Enteric bacteria like E. coli can thrive in hyperosmotic environments compared to most laboratory growth media by maintaining the periplasm and the cytoplasm in an iso-osmotic state (Ingraham and Marr, 1996; Stock et al., 1977).
source: Enteric bacteria like E. coli can thrive in hyperosmotic environments compared to most laboratory growth media, such as the human gut by maintaining the periplasm and the cytoplasm in an iso-osmotic state (Ingraham and Marr, 1996; Stock et al., 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: The periplasmic volume increased rapidly in response to increased osmolyte levels in the external medium, which can reduce the cytoplasmic volume by about 30% and substantially increase the periplasmic volume by around 300% (Stock et al., 1977; Cayley et al., 2000; Pilizota and Shaevitz, 2013).
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that the periplasmic volume increased rapidly in response to increased osmolyte levels in the external medium. This phenomenon can reduce the cytoplasmic volume by about 30%, thereby constricting the IM inwards, and substantially increasing the periplasmic volume by around 300% (Stock et al., 1977; Cayley et al., 2000; Pilizota and Shaevitz, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior published work.

claim: On minimal growth medium, growth rates of the Lpp+21 strain of E. coli were equivalent to the isogenic wild-type E. coli.
source: On minimal growth medium, growth rates of the Lpp+21 strain of E. coli were equivalent to the isogenic wild-type E. coli (Figure 1C).

claim: Growth rates of Lpp+21 strain were equivalent to wild-type on growth media osmotically balanced with concentrations of sorbitol up to 1.0 M.
source: This was likewise true on growth media osmotically balanced with concentrations of sorbitol up to 1.0 M (Figure 1D)

source: and on rich (LB) medium with or without sorbitol (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the growth curve data presented in Figure 1D.

claim: The average distance from the middle of the IM density to the middle of the OM density was increased in both wild-type and Lpp+21 strains under hyperosmotic conditions when compared to previously reported data where cells were grown in standard laboratory media (Asmar et al., 2017).
source: As expected, the average distance from the middle of the IM density to the middle of the OM density was increased in both strains under hyperosmotic conditions when compared to previously reported data where cells were grown in standard laboratory media (Asmar et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by the electron cryotomography data and comparison to prior published work.

claim: The averaged distance from the IM to the OM were somewhat greater in the Lpp+21 strain (32–36 nm) compared to the isogenic wild-type strain (30–32 nm).
source: As shown in Figure 1E, the averaged distance from the IM to the OM were somewhat greater in the Lpp+21 strain (32–36 nm) compared to the isogenic wild-type strain (30–32 nm) in line with previous Lpp+21 periplasmic width measurements.
evidence: This claim is supported by the electron cryotomography measurements presented in Figure 1E.

claim: The distance to the center of the PG density from the OM was slightly increased in the Lpp+21 strain, although by less than the anticipated ~3 nm.
source: The distance to the center of the PG density from the OM was slightly increased in the Lpp+21 strain (Figure 1F), although by less than the anticipated ~3 nm.

claim: In the wild-type strain a uniform dark PG layer could be observed in the images, whereas in the Lpp+21 strain a broader and more diffuse PG layer was evident, suggesting heterogeneity in both the density and thickness of the PG.
source: The PG morphology was also qualitatively different: in the wild-type strain a uniform dark PG layer could be observed in the images, whereas in the Lpp+21 strain a broader and more diffuse PG layer was evident, suggesting heterogeneity in both the density and thickness of the PG.
evidence: This claim is supported by the electron cryotomography images and analysis.

claim: The level of the oligopeptide transporter subunits (OppB, OppC, OppD and OppF) are substantially increased in the Lpp+21 strain compared to the wild-type.
source: The level of the oligopeptide transporter subunits (OppB, OppC, OppD and OppF) are substantially increased in the Lpp+21 strain compared to the wild-type (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the quantitative proteomics data.

claim: The increase in oligopeptide transporter subunits suggests an increase in PG turnover and an overall increased capacity to recycle PG components.
source: This suggests an increase in PG turnover and an overall increased capacity to recycle PG components and is consistent with the concomitant increase in AmiC, one of the two major amidases involved in PG remodeling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the proteomics data showing increased oligopeptide transporter levels.
